summary_html: A child dies or suffers serious harm while **under agency supervision**, constituting systemic failure. Federal law mandates disclosure and review to identify causes and reforms.
authority_html:
- **Protect Our Kids Act (PL 112-275)** — federal commission and review requirements  
- **CAPTA §5106a(b)(2)(A)(x)** — mandates public disclosure of child-fatality cases

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Cline v. State, Department of Family Services
key_cases.holding: In wrongful-death suits arising from the deaths of two teenagers placed by the State in a private 24-hour care facility, the Court affirmed summary judgment for the State, holding the facility was an independent contractor and neither it nor its employee was a 'public employee' whose torts the Governmental Claims Act would reach.
key_cases.relevance: Certification and regulatory oversight of a placement provider do not, without operational control, make the State answerable for the provider's negligence.
key_cases.quote: as a matter of law, NSI was an independent contractor, and neither NSI nor its employee Edward Gillison was a “public employee” under the Claims Act

key_cases.case_name: DeShaney v. Winnebago County Department of Social Services
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a State's failure to protect a child from private violence, even after the agency received repeated reports and took no action, does not violate the Due Process Clause, because the Clause imposes no affirmative duty of protection absent a custodial relationship.
key_cases.relevance: Sets the constitutional baseline against which liability for a child's death after agency contact is measured, and marks the custody exception that Tenth Circuit foster-care cases build on.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that a State's failure to protect an individual against private violence simply does not constitute a violation of the Due Process Clause

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Tenth Circuit recognized that a foster child harmed by the State may sue under the special-relationship doctrine, but reversed the denial of qualified immunity because it was not clearly established that out-of-state caseworkers had a special relationship with a child placed across state lines.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies the special-relationship elements a family must plead when a child is injured or dies under agency supervision.
key_cases.quote: When a state fails to protect a foster child from harm, the foster child can sue the state under the special-relationship doctrine

state_agency.name: Wyoming Department of Family Services
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the DFS field office in the county where the child lives — the list is at dfs.wyo.gov/about/contact-us

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Entry of the appealable juvenile court order, judgment or decree (Wyo. Stat. § 14-3-432(a) applies the Wyoming Rules of Appellate Procedure; W.R.A.P. 2.01(a) sets the 30 days)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Timely filing of a notice of appeal is jurisdictional (W.R.A.P. 1.03(a))
